title: Queued spillover sweep (scratchpad)
content:
Objective:
- Quick sweep of queued-spillover strategies to understand tail-latency behavior during microbursts and long-tailed loads.
- Compare three policies: no-spill (baseline), soft-spill (gradual offload to spare GPU pool), aggressive-spill (early offload to CPU fallback + thin quantized variant).

Context / motivation:
- Recent customer report (INF-482) saw p99s jump during 30–90s microbursts despite ample total capacity. Hypothesis: local queueing + conservative preemption causes long service times for some requests (k-v cache warm misses amplify). We want a small-run exploratory matrix to pick candidates for longer A/B.

Testbed / env:
- Model: rwd-gpt-small-v1 (12B-ish architecture, non-opt float, quantized path available)
- Hardware: single A100-80GB served by runtime v2.11.3; spare pool: 2xA100 for spill targets; CPU fallback nodes: 4x8-core w/ int8 quant variant.
- Runtime settings: kvcache enabled, prefix-caching TTL 60s, batching dynamic, max-batch=32, max-concurrency=64
- Arrival patterns: baseline Poisson (lambda -> 80 qps), microburst injection (30s pulse at 600 qps every 10 min), long-tailed (Pareto with alpha=1.8 for 20m window)
- Payload: median prompt length 120 tokens, generation 64 tokens
- Measurement windows: warm (first 5 min ignored), run for 2h per config, sample every 10s buckets for latency distribution, track per-token cost estimate and queue depth histogram

Policies tested:
1) baseline-no-spill: runtime buffers up to queue_limit=500 requests, no offload; preemptive eviction disabled
2) soft-spill: if queue_depth > 0.7*queue_limit, route 20% of new arrivals to spare GPU pool; attempt kvcache sharing (best-effort)
3) aggressive-spill: if queue_depth > 0.5*queue_limit, immediate offload to CPU fallback (quantized model) for low-priority workloads; preemption enabled to free up slot for high-priority traffic

Key metrics captured:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms)
- throughput (req/s served by each tier)
- spill_rate (% of requests offloaded)
- cold-kvcache-miss-rate (% requests missing k-v cache)
- error-rate (5xx)

Raw summarized results (2h each):
- baseline-no-spill:
  p50: 45ms, p90: 120ms, p95: 185ms, p99: 820ms
  throughput sustained: 580 req/s during bursts, average across run 150 req/s
  spill_rate: 0%
  cold-kvcache-miss-rate: 37% (amp during bursts)
  5xx: 0.06%

- soft-spill:
  p50: 48ms, p90: 130ms, p95: 190ms, p99: 420ms
  throughput sustained: 610 req/s during bursts, avg 165 req/s
  spill_rate: 12% (mostly to spare GPU pool)
  cold-kvcache-miss-rate: 29%
  5xx: 0.03%

- aggressive-spill:
  p50: 55ms, p90: 170ms, p95: 240ms, p99: 290ms
  throughput sustained: 630 req/s (including CPU fallback), avg 170 req/s
  spill_rate: 34% (mix CPU fallback + quantized variant)
  cold-kvcache-miss-rate: 18% (less amplification since fewer stuck requests)
  5xx: 0.12% (some errors from quantized path during warmup)

Quick ASCII latency trend (p99) sample across a single burst window (time -> 0..30s):
- baseline: 100,120,160,210,300,520,760,820,780,640,410,260,160,120,105,95,90,88,86,85,84,83,82,81,80,79,78,77,76,75
- soft-spill: 90,95,100,110,150,200,320,420,360,300,230,180,140,110,105,100,98,97,95,93,92,91,90,89,88,87,86,85,84,83
- aggressive-spill: 95,100,110,130,160,200,230,290,270,250,220,200,190,180,170,165,160,158,155,152,150,148,146,145,144,143,142,140,138,135

Observations / interpretations:
- Baseline experiences severe p99 spikes (up to ~820ms) caused by queue head-of-line blocking + kvcache warm misses during bursts. These long tails persist for tens of seconds.
- Soft-spill meaningfully reduces spike amplitude (p99 cut ~50%) and decreases kvcache misses, likely because fewer requests queue long enough to miss cache warm windows. Minimal capacity overhead.
- Aggressive-spill reduces p99 further and stabilizes profile, but shifts some load to quantized CPU path which slightly increases p50/p90 and introduces a higher 5xx rate during ramp (quantized path warmups flaky). Also higher spill_rate means more variant mismatch risk (quality difference).

Practical tradeoffs:
- Soft-spill gives the best win/cost compromise for latency-sensitive endpoints that can tolerate small fraction offloaded to identical model hardware.
- Aggressive-spill is useful for hard SLOs on p99 if variance in output quality between GPU and CPU paths is acceptable and error handling for quantized warmups is improved.

Short TODOs / next steps:
- Re-run aggressive-spill with improved quantized warmup (PR #1182 has a heuristic; run 1h smoke) -> reduced 5xx expected.
- Add a config that does kvcache prefetching to spare pool when soft-spill routing triggers (should further reduce cold misses).
- Run A/B with a real customer traffic replay (INF-482) to validate signal.
- Add per-tenant analysis (some tenants had much worse amplification; correlate prompt length & cache affinity).

Notes to self:
- Watch out for measurement bias: sample windows should exclude initial 2m after policy flip to avoid transient artifacts.
- Document tradeoff matrix for product: p50 vs p99 vs quality vs unit-cost. This will be useful for console recommendation UX in Optimize.

Linked quick figures (copied into GH comment later):
- "burst_p99_traces.png" (generated)
- "spill_rate_over_time.csv" (raw)

End of scratchpad.
